# Evidence designed to be reused

<p class="inner-lede">Historical data construction is part of the substantive contribution. Each public project documents coverage, source logic, transformations, and limitations so that the evidence can be inspected beyond a single regression table.</p>
:::

## Measuring Financial Stress under the Gold Standard

<p class="dataset-summary">A monthly dataset and composite index designed to recover the chronology of monetary, banking, and macro-financial pressure in interwar Czechoslovakia.</p>

::: {.dataset-metrics}
::: {.metric}
<span class="metric-value">11</span>
<span class="metric-label">component indicators</span>
:::
::: {.metric}
<span class="metric-value">107</span>
<span class="metric-label">monthly observations</span>
:::
::: {.metric}
<span class="metric-value">1929:11</span>
<span class="metric-label">series begins</span>
:::
::: {.metric}
<span class="metric-value">1938:09</span>
<span class="metric-label">series ends</span>
:::
:::

::: {.dataset-columns}
::: {}
### Research use

- identifying distinct phases of financial pressure;
- comparing market, monetary, and real-economy chronologies;
- evaluating conventional dates assigned to the Czechoslovak Depression;
- studying monetary defence before and after devaluation.
:::
::: {}
### Package contents

- underlying monthly indicators;
- transformed and standardised series;
- composite financial-stress measure;
- documentation and replication materials;
- transparent versioned DOI.
:::
:::

[Open project and download data](https://doi.org/10.3886/E247312V1){.button .button-primary}
:::
:::

## Commercial Hysteresis in European Trade

<p class="dataset-summary">A bilateral panel for tracing persistence, destruction, and reorganisation in Europe’s commercial relationships across the Great Depression.</p>

::: {.dataset-metrics}
::: {.metric}
<span class="metric-value">21</span>
<span class="metric-label">European economies</span>
:::
::: {.metric}
<span class="metric-value">12</span>
<span class="metric-label">annual cross-sections</span>
:::
::: {.metric}
<span class="metric-value">1927</span>
<span class="metric-label">pre-crisis benchmark</span>
:::
::: {.metric}
<span class="metric-value">1938</span>
<span class="metric-label">late-interwar endpoint</span>
:::
:::

::: {.dataset-columns}
::: {}
### Research use

- separating aggregate trade collapse from link-level persistence;
- mapping partner substitution and regional reorientation;
- estimating intensive- and extensive-margin adjustment;
- studying the effects of exchange and clearing regimes.
:::
::: {}
### Unit of observation

The core unit is the directional country-pair-year. That structure permits exporter, importer, pair, and time effects while preserving the geography of commercial adjustment.
:::
:::

[Open project and download data](https://doi.org/10.3886/E247132V2){.button .button-primary}

## Nordic Trade Resilience

<p class="dataset-summary">Public replication materials for “Reassessing Nordic Trade Resilience during the Great Depression: A Bilateral Decomposition of European Trade Flows, 1927–1938.”</p>

The project examines Nordic trade performance within the wider reorganisation of European bilateral commerce during the Great Depression. The openICPSR deposit provides data and code for the analysis.

[Open replication package](https://doi.org/10.3886/E251239V1){.button .button-primary}
:::
:::

::: {.page-section}
<p class="eyebrow">In development</p>

## Wider Czechoslovak data programme

The public packages sit within a broader effort to consolidate scattered evidence on the interwar Czechoslovak economy. These components are under active construction and will be released only when their provenance and transformations are sufficiently documented.

::: {.pipeline-grid}
::: {.pipeline-card}
<span class="pipeline-status">Building</span>

### Monthly macro-financial database

Central-bank balance sheets, currency and reserves, prices, industrial activity, labour-market indicators, trade, and bilateral exchange rates.
:::

::: {.pipeline-card}
<span class="pipeline-status">Reconstructing</span>

### Agricultural output and national income

Crop quantities, livestock, prices, value added, and explicit assumptions for linking sectoral reconstruction to broader output estimates.
:::

::: {.pipeline-card}
<span class="pipeline-status">Harmonising</span>

### District-level Czechoslovakia

Population, occupational structure, social and political indicators, and electoral outcomes for the 1920s and 1930s.
:::
:::
:::

::: {.principles-band}
<p class="eyebrow light">Replication principles</p>

## A dataset should expose its judgement calls

::: {.principles-grid}
::: {}
### Provenance
Every series should be traceable to an archival table, statistical publication, or documented secondary reconstruction.
:::
::: {}
### Transformations
Deflation, interpolation, seasonal adjustment, harmonisation, and index construction should be visible rather than buried.
:::
::: {}
### Uncertainty
Alternative assumptions and fragile links belong in the package, not only in private working files.
:::
::: {}
### Versioning
Stable repositories and versioned DOIs make it possible to distinguish a cited release from later improvements.
:::
:::
:::
